subject: LLM response integrity — NovaCorp incident update & remediation plan
messages:
From: Amy Wu <amy.wu@novacorp.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Weird corrupted responses from your API (production)

Hi Aisha —

We're seeing a stream of responses from Redwood's /v1/generate endpoint that contain truncated JSON and repeated token fragments. This started around 08:45 PDT and is affecting ~5% of requests across two of our services. Attached is a small sample (error_samples.txt) with request IDs and redacted inputs.

Impact: downstream parsing fails, which causes our ingestion workers to drop messages; blocking several downstream jobs. This is high priority for us.

Can you confirm you're looking into this? We can provide more samples or enable extra logging on our side.

Thanks,
Amy
Amy Wu
Head of Platform Integrations
NovaCorp

Attachment: error_samples.txt

Immediate actions: 
- We've opened PD-23419 and are standing a bridge (link below).
- Evelyn (SRE) is investigating logs and model routing; Ben (your account lead) is coordinating priorities.
- If you can share any recently changed client-side settings (model name, max_tokens, streaming options), that will help narrow scope.

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 10:22:03 -0700
Subject: RE: Stand-up: NovaCorp bridge (PD-23419)

Quick technical update (initial triage):
- Root cause hypothesis: an encoding edge-case in the tokenization path for concatenated prompt headers + long user context when using the new batched streaming runtime. Under certain token boundary conditions we saw duplicated byte sequences injected into the output buffer before finalization. This manifests as repeated fragments and sometimes invalid JSON for structured-output customers.
- Scope: impacts requests to the rdx-large-v2 family with streaming enabled and context length > 8k tokens; observed in ~4.8% of NovaCorp requests (samples attached).
- Mitigation (in progress): 1) temporarily route affected traffic to rdx-large-v1 (stable variant) for NovaCorp; 2) disable streaming assembly optimization for their tenant for the next 24 hours while we patch the tokenizer finalization. We're implementing a route policy now and will monitor error rates.
- Next steps: patch ready by EOD PT, staged rollforward after internal QA. We'll provide a permanent fix and a postmortem.

I've attached the bridge logs (bridge_logs.zip) and included request IDs that map to the samples Amy provided. I'll update in 60 minutes with metrics after the routing change.

Evelyn
SRE, Runtime Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: bridge_logs.zip

Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 16:41:00 -0700
Subject: Final update: NovaCorp LLM response integrity incident — follow-up and next steps

Amy — following up with the executive-facing summary, remediation timeline, and our commitments. Thank you for your patience while our teams worked through the issue. Below is a concise summary we will share with your leadership if helpful.

Summary of incident:
- What happened: Under a narrow tokenization boundary condition in our new streaming assembly optimization, repeated byte fragments could be injected into response buffers for long-context streaming requests, leading to malformed outputs in a minority of requests.
- Impact window: 2026-05-04 08:45 PT -> 2026-05-04 11:05 PT (errors rate peaked ~4.8% for NovaCorp calls to rdx-large-v2 streaming).
- Customers affected: NovaCorp (partial traffic), isolated to rdx-large-v2 streaming path.

Remediation taken:
- Immediate: routed NovaCorp to rdx-large-v1 at 10:00 PT on 2026-05-04; disabled streaming assembly optimization for your tenant. Error rate reduced to <0.05% within 45 minutes.
- Short-term: patch to the tokenizer finalization committed and deployed to canary cluster 2026-05-04 18:20 PT; monitoring results look good.
- Long-term: we will add an additional validation step for streaming assembly and expand automated regression tests to cover concatenated prompt header edge-cases.

Customer commitments:
- Action: We will provide a full postmortem and remediation plan within 72 hours (link below).
- Credit: We are issuing a service credit equivalent to 10% of NovaCorp's May usage to account for outage impact; Ben will coordinate billing adjustment.
- Security: No evidence of data exfiltration; malformed outputs did not leave customer data in logs beyond usual request metadata. Our security team will provide a signed statement if you need it for compliance.

Attachments and links:
- Draft postmortem: postmortem-draft.md
- Action tracker for follow-ups: customer_followup_actions.csv
- Incident runbook / PD: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-23419
- JIRA: SUP-3421 (tracking the fix and regression tests)

Next steps / owner list:
- Ben Carter: coordinate customer billing credit and communications
- Marcus Lin: confirm regression suite and QA schedule (owner for rollforward validation)
- Evelyn Hart: lead runtime patch validation and add monitoring alerts
- Aisha Rahman: primary point of contact for NovaCorp exec updates

If you'd like, I can join a 30-minute call with your ops and security teams tomorrow to walk through the postmortem.

Appreciate your partnership,

Aisha Rahman
Account Director, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: postmortem-draft.md, customer_followup_actions.csv
